newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hongkong Land expects flat 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Land expects flat 1997 earnings.

text.p: Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd reported a leap in 1996 profits to US$649.4 million on Wednesday but warned this year's earnings were likely to be flat as leases signed at peak levels three years ago came up for renegotiation.

The profits after tax and minority interests figure for the year ended December 31, 1996, was a huge increase over the US$256.9 million the company posted in 1995 -- buoyed mainly by a writeback of US$217 million from the sale of its stake in Trafalgar House Plc.
The company said if the Trafalgar House effect for the past two years was excluded, its net profit grew by four percent to US$432 million from US$415 million in 1995.
"Earnings in the current year are expected to be flat," chairman Simon Keswick was quoted as saying in a statement.

Because most of the leases on the company's Hong Kong retail and office space were for three years, the prices on renewals this year were likely to be lower than those signed in 1994, when the territory's property market was peaking, managing director Percy Weatherall told Reuters by telephone.
The company also warned that new developments near its properties in the bustling Central district would be completed in 1998, adding to direct competition.

Hongkong Land said it was considering the feasibility of redeveloping Swire House, a 427,000 square foot commercial property in the heart of Hong Kong's business district and would make a final decision before the end of 1997.
Keswick said progress made in expanding regional property and infrastructure interests would provide the basis for longer-term growth.
Hong Kong-managed but Singapore-listed Hongkong Land holds the vast majority of its property interests in Hong Kong.
It is 32 percent-owned by Jardine Strategic Holdings Ltd, which is 60 percent-owned by Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd.
Hongkong Land said net income from properties rose to US$485.1 million in 1996 from US$465.6 million the year before.
Its property revaluation reserve swelled to US$8.177 billion at December 31, up from US$6.113 billion.
While the company's earnings have tended to stem from its high-quality property portfolio, it expanded its regional activities in 1996.
"We've said we'd be more active, and I think we have been more active," Weatherall said, pointing to investments in the Philippines, China, Vietnam and Indonesia.
He said the company would continue to look for good opportunities both in property and infrastructure.
Last year, Hongkong Land successfully tendered for a prime commercial site in Singapore, and is involved in two projects in the Philippines.
In September it took a US$30 million interest in Indonesian toll road operator PT Marga Mandalasakti.
In Vietnam, Hongkong Land's first Hanoi investment was almost fully let and construction of a second office development was well underway, it said.
The company said it made progress last year in resolving delayed development of new facilities at Hong Kong's Kwai Chung container port.
Hongkong Land has a 23 percent stake in Kwai Chung Container Terminals and is in talks to operate two berths at Container Terminal 8.
